subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno was recruiting badly and aggressively, pulling individuals from the Earth Temple's side one frightened bugbear at a time, and his actions triggered a three-way war.

subject: Dren
fact: Dren stepped up with his two mercenaries and seized Calmer, dragging him back through the corridor after the cleric was rendered ineffective by necrotic damage and depleted healing capacity.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer was a cleric reduced to three hit points, his healing well scraped dry and his body still saturated with necrotic cold from a wraith; he could no longer sustain himself and was deemed an unusable resource in the skirmish.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a combatant whose wit has grown sharper as the party delves deeper into the temple; he made dry observations about the gnolls' motivations and later delivered lethal strikes against them.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is a companion who finished off the first slain gnoll after the initial strike from concealment, demonstrating coordinated lethality in ambush tactics.

subject: Air Temple Gnolls
fact: The Air Temple gnolls are a group acting collectively with predatory intent, having invested in purchased defections and now seeking reimbursement and sustenance after their investment was destroyed.

subject: Gnoll (first)
fact: A gnoll was slain by a strike from concealment, the dagger finding the soft place under the ribs; it folded mostly to dead in a single beat, and Zinnia finished what remained.

subject: Gnoll (second)
fact: A gnoll was killed by Sequoia after being tagged cleanly and opened up; it had nothing left to lose and died without resistance.

subject: Gnoll (third)
fact: The final gnoll was dispatched by the narrator with a high-low-blindsided dagger strike; it didn't so much die as stop, earning no eulogy beyond its role as an attacker.

subject: ambush of the Air Temple Gnolls
fact: An ambush was executed in the corridor of the Air Temple, resulting in the elimination of three gnolls; the party exploited stealth and concealment to neutralize the threat with minimal damage to themselves.

subject: Air Temple Corridor
fact: The corridor is a narrow, ugly brown-and-black space where the ambush occurred; it leads to a secret door that opens into an unknown area, now controlled by the party.

subject: Secret Door
fact: The secret door coughed up replacements during the ambush and now hangs open, providing access to an unexplored route — possibly leading to the Water Temple, though officially it connects to the Air Temple.

subject: Coins
fact: The coins were pocketed as both evidence and payment; they were left behind by the gnolls and taken as spoils of the skirmish.

subject: missing healer
fact: With Calmer incapacitated and unusable, the party lacks a healer; this creates a critical vulnerability for any further operations into the stronghold beyond the secret door.

subject: unknown route beyond the door
fact: The secret door opens into an unexplored path; its destination is uncertain, but the party must now decide whether to attempt a recon mission without a healer.

subject: tiefling as prey
fact: The gnoll recognized the narrator as a tiefling and expressed desire to consume their flesh; this reinforces a recurring theme: the narrator's existence is perceived as a resource to be exploited by hostile entities.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during a session in which the party engaged in stealth-based combat, eliminated three gnolls, and shifted their objective from assault to reconnaissance.
